rows.name: Local Poke Bowl
rows.description: Poke bowl vendor named at the Thursday Haleiwa farmers market in 2025
rows.source_label: Hawaii News Now story (not re-opened in this pass)
rows.notes: No current vendor, organizer or own page confirms this vendor. The only 2025 source is the March 2025 Hawaii News Now story, which I could not re-open; it named them at the Thursday market. A Haleiwa Town guide (late 2025) says the FarmLovers Haleiwa market is temporarily closed. FarmLovers' own page and a HI Now page still list a Thursday Haleiwa market but disagree on place (59-864 Kamehameha Hwy at Waimea Valley vs 66-434 Kamehameha Hwy) and hours (2-6 vs 3-7 summer); neither lists this vendor. Neighborhood set to null because it came only from the market; a 2024 Hawaii News Now story calls the owner a Waialua chef, so the vendor's base is unconfirmed (side north_shore comes from the market and the chef's home area). That 2024 story also confirms the Instagram handle @localpokebowl and an email (localpokebowl@gmail.com, not a schema field), and said they were at Pearlridge's Village Night Market on Saturday evenings. That is pre-2025, so I did not list it as a market. Whether they still sell anywhere is unknown. Verify with the vendor before publishing.

rows.name: Mochi Lab
rows.description: Stuffed butter mochi sold at farmers markets; catering offered
rows.notes: Their Facebook page is undated. It lists Wednesday Blaisdell 4-7pm and Thursday Kailua 5-7:30pm, offers catering and custom orders, and has a post saying they are at KCC every Saturday until 11am. The phone number and mochilab808@gmail.com (not a schema field) are on the page. The page's Blaisdell address belongs to the market, so address is null. The page says Honolulu and gives no neighborhood. The Hawaii Farm Bureau's KCC page (about Aug 2026) lists other mochi vendors, but the part I saw does not include Mochi Lab. Honolulu Magazine's 'At the Market' feature on them is years old (pre-2025, not usable), and the Kailua hours on the Facebook page look stale. I found no 2025-or-later source or current organizer list showing them selling, so active status is unconfirmed. Check with the business or the organizer before publishing. A different Mochi Lab in Toronto is unrelated.

rows.name: Ohana Style Snack Co.
rows.description: Island-flavor snacks: jerky chips, guava beef jerky, popcorn; online orders
rows.notes: Their own site lists the Campbell Avenue store address, but also says online orders only at this time, so walk-in pickup is not confirmed. The Big Cartel store lists the jerky chips, guava beef jerky and popcorn flavors; cotton candy and fruit roll-ups come from their Eventeny vendor profile. The Honolulu Festival organizer's page lists them for 2024, 2025 and 2026 (30th), which supports active status. The Hawaii Holiday Craft & Gift Fair listing from the first pass could not be confirmed from any organizer page, so markets is empty. Neighborhood and side are null because the own site says only Honolulu 96815. Prices are left out. They are not the California business Ohana Bros.

rows.name: Paige's Pretty Patterns
rows.description: Student maker listed in Mākia Market's Aug 2026 festival booth slot
rows.notes: The article lists Paige Hijirida (class of 2033) in the first evening slot (6:30-10pm, Thursday Aug 20) of Mākia Market's booth 106 at the Made in Hawaiʻi Festival (Aug 20-23, 2026, Hawaiʻi Convention Center). That event has passed. Products are not stated. Mākia Market's own pages (makiaco.com, Fall 2025 event page) say its makers markets are held at The Barn at SALT at Our Kakaʻako on select dates, but this vendor is not named on those pages. The vendor's base, neighborhood and any own page are unknown, so those fields are null. Whether the vendor is still active is unknown.

rows.name: Saszdcreations
rows.description: Handmade totes, mini baskets and monstera pillow covers
rows.source_label: KHON2 story on the fair (date approximate, from its age)
rows.notes: The KHON2 story (about late Oct 2025, approximate) on the Hawaii Holiday Craft & Gift Fair at the Blaisdell Center (Oct 31-Nov 2, 2025) names owner Dana Rickard and shows handmade bags. An older KHON2 story (about Nov 2024) spelled the surname Devers and listed totes, mini baskets and monstera pillow covers; Rickard is the later spelling. Kaneohe comes from another maker's page (Just 4U by Kawena A.), which says Dana of Saszdcreations is from Kaneohe and sends orders to saszdcreations.com. I could not open the vendor's own website or current posts. The 2026 fair (Oct 30-Nov 1) has not been confirmed for this vendor. Instagram handle is from the first pass; the bio gives Saszdcreations@yahoo.com (not a schema field).

rows.name: Weirdoughs
rows.description: Focaccia sandwiches and flatbreads; may no longer operate under this name
products: Hot n' weird panini pressed sandwiches
rows.source_label: Hana Kitchens' member list (the commissary's own page)
rows.notes: Hana Kitchens' current homepage still lists Weirdoughs as a member, but that does not show it is selling. Honolulu Magazine's tag page says owner Aaron Biolos is 'formerly known for' WeirDoughs and now makes sandwiches at The Local General Store in Kaimukī (undated). The Local General Store appears on the Hawaii Farm Bureau's current KCC vendor list. I found no source showing Weirdoughs selling at the Honolulu Farmers' Market, so markets is empty and the earlier Kakaʻako neighborhood is removed. The Marketspread vendor profile (undated) gives the product list and an Aiea, HI location, but no market is named. An old Honolulu Magazine item mentions Thursday-morning pop-ups at Hana Kitchens (undated). I could not verify an Instagram handle. Active status is unconfirmed, and the brand may have ended. Check with the business or Hana Kitchens.
